lines: vaines ſupperſtitions, & autres telles choſes inutilles. {d}
Ledit du Tilh ouy ſur cet enſorcelle-
ment & malefice, nom de preſtres, & ce-
remonies gardées, reſpond en tout
comme ladite de Rols, ſans en rien fail-
lir, adiouſter, ni diminuer. Procedant
aux confrontemẽs, iceluy du Tilh requi-
ert que ladite de Rols ſoit miſe en ſeque
ſtre, & liberté, pour euiter ſubornation:
ce qui eſt ordonné, & executé.
Nous auons monſtré ci deſſus, que la ſequeſtration
des biens, & plus encor des perſonnes, eſt odieuſe &
prohibée: ſi ce n'eſt pour quelque grande & legitime
cauſe, comme eſt en ce faict la crainte de ſeduction, &
ſubornation. {a}
Les confrontemens paracheuez, &
baillez reproches par ledit du Tilh, &
requeſte, pour luy eſtre permis publier
monitoire, ſur les articles y attachez
concernans la pretendue ſubornation
de ladite de Rols. Par ordõnance il eſt
receu à verifier les reproches par luy
deduits. Et neantmoins, attẽdu la matie
re dont eſt queſtion, faire publier led.
monitoire, pour mieux ſçauoir la verité:
& ordõné, ſera enquis d'office, tant aux
lieux du Pin, Sagias, & Artigat, que a au-
tres circõuoiſins, & neceſſaires, tãt ſur la
l. ij. §. ſi ve
rò vtraque.
D. de lib. ex-
hib. c. ex tran
miſſa. c. literas
de reſtit. ſpol.
c. penul. de
probã.

uncertain.text: vaines ſupperſtitions, & autres telles choſes inutilles. {d}
uncertain.note: marker {d} has no note anywhere on this page: margin-1.jpg is blank beside and above this line (only the folio 44 stands there), the only margin note on the page is keyed a and stands 40 lines lower, and foot.jpg shows no foot citation block. The letter is a clear italic d at 4x (body-1.jpg, x~1620), and it follows p044's last marker c, which likewise had no note. Marker recorded without a note; the reconciler should check whether the printer dropped both citations.

uncertain.text: vaines ſupperſtitions, & autres telles choſes inutilles. {d}
uncertain.note: the mark between 'inutilles' and the marker is a round dot on the baseline (period), checked at 4x against the commas of 'ſupperſtitions,' on the same line, which show a clear descending tail. Transcribed 'inutilles. {d}', the printed order kept.

sic: the second sort is an F, not an E. At 4x (body-1.jpg, y~415) it has a top arm and a middle arm and no bottom arm, whereas the fifth sort of the same word is a full three-armed E, as is every letter of the 'TEXTE.' heading lower on this page (body-4.jpg). A wrong sort in the compositor's stick; transcribed as printed, not corrected to TEXTE.

two oddities, both transcribed as printed. (a) the mark after ANNOTAT is a comma with a clear descending tail at 4x, not the point this head usually takes. (b) the numeral is X X I I I I (counted at 7x: two X's then four plain serifed I's, no further stroke), i.e. XXIIII = 24 — the same number as p044's 'ANNOT. XXIIII.'. Either p044's head or this one is a misprint; this page's head also spells ANNOTAT in full where p044 has ANNOT. Spaced capitals closed up per §3.

uncertain.text: aux confrontemẽs, iceluy du Tilh requi-
uncertain.note: the diacritic over the second e is a tilde, not an acute. At 9x (body-3.jpg, x~440) it is a flat, nearly horizontal bar sitting close on the letter, the same shape as the tildes of 'attẽdu' and 'ordõnance' (body-6.jpg); this fount's acute, as on 'liberté', 'gardées', 'executé', is a steeply slanted stroke set high and clear of the letter. Read 'confrontemẽs' (= confrontemens), which the sense also wants; the word is set in full as 'confrontemens' at blocks[6].lines[0].

printed 'lir , adio uſter, ni' — a justification space before the comma, normalized away per §1, and a full word space inside 'adiouſter', joined per §1 (the same case as 'l'anné e' on an earlier page). No hyphen or other mark stands in the gap at 5x.

a wide justification space is printed before the comma ('gardées , reſpond'); normalized away per §1. Same at blocks[6].lines[1] ('Tilh , &'), blocks[6].lines[3] ('monitoire , ſur'), blocks[6].lines[8] ('queſtion , faire'), blocks[6].lines[10] ('d'office ,tant') and blocks[4].lines[1] ('biens , &', 'perſonnes , eſt').

uncertain.text: cauſe, comme eſt en ce faict la crainte de ſeduction, &
uncertain.note: no space is printed after the comma ('cauſe,comme'); normalized per §1. Same at blocks[6].lines[7] ('neantmoins,attẽdu'), blocks[6].lines[9] ('monitoire,pour'), blocks[6].lines[10] ('ordõné,ſera'), blocks[6].lines[11] ('Pin,Sagias', 'Artigat,que') and blocks[6].lines[12] ('neceſſaires,tãt').

a small pale mark sits over the second e of 'paracheuez' (body-5.jpg, y~20). At 5x it is brown and much lighter than the type, unlike the firmly inked tildes and acutes elsewhere on the page; read as a speck or show-through, so a plain e. Reading otherwise secure.

the third sort is read as the paragraph sign §. It is heavily over-inked (margin-2.jpg, x~400, y~630): at 10x with unsharp it shows a small loop open to the left at the top, a dark middle, a second loop at the bottom and a short tail running down-left, which is this italic's §; a capital B would show a straight vertical stem on the left, which is absent. The citation formula (l. ij. §. ſi verò vtraque, D. de lib. exhib. = Dig. 43.30, de liberis exhibendis) also wants a §. Reader B should check the glyph independently.

the line-end mark after 'ex' is a short stroke set at x-height (margin-2.jpg, x~540, y~770; seen at 10x normalized). Read as the word-break sign for 'ex|hib', transcribed as a single '-' per §1. It is the only such mark at the right edge of this note that sits on a line whose word is broken.

one or two small dark specks stand high to the right of the final s of 'literas' (margin-2.jpg, x~575, y~885), above x-height. They are far higher than this fount's periods (compare 'vtraque.' on lines[1] and 'ſpol.' on lines[5], both on the baseline) and have no comma tail, so no punctuation is transcribed after 'literas'. If reader B reads a raised comma there the reconciler should decide. The double s of 'miſſa' is ſſ: both sorts are tall with descenders at 14x.

sic: the word breaks 'tran|miſſa' with no hyphen and without the s of 'transmissa' (c. Ex transmissa). Transcribed as printed; the print's narrow points ('hib.c.ex') are spaced per §1. Likewise 'l.ij.' on lines[0] and 'miſſa.c.literas' on lines[4].

placement: this is the page's only margin note, and it has drifted a long way down from its marker. Its first line stands in the white band between the last body line of the ANNOTAT paragraph ('ſubornation. {a}') and the 'TEXTE.' heading below it; its remaining seven lines run down beside the first six lines of the last paragraph, ending beside 'concernans la pretendue ſubornation'. The key letter is an unambiguous italic a at 8x. beside_line is given as the marker's own line.

uncertain.note: last line of the page; the sentence runs on to p046, hence continues_next. foot.jpg is blank below it: no foot citation block, no signature and no catchword. 'circõuoiſins' is printed 'circõuoiſin s' with a gap before the final s, joined per §1; 'neceſſaires' is ſſ (both sorts tall, checked at 5x).

uncertain.text: lieux du Pin, Sagias, & Artigat, que a au-
uncertain.note: sic: 'que a' is printed with a word space and no apostrophe (compare 'qu'elle' elsewhere in the book); no mark is visible between the e and the space at 5x.

uncertain.text: Nous auons monſtré ci deſſus, que la ſequeſtration
uncertain.note: 'deſſus' is ſſ, not ſs: at 5x both sorts are tall long s with the ſſ ligature's shared top (body-4.jpg, x~850). Checked because §7 of the reader brief flags this class.
